title: Khalifah The Fisherman Of Baghdad (Español)
summary: Khalifah was an impoverished, merry fisherman of Baghdad who lived in a ruined hut and owned only a patched net and a single linen tunic ... [ES]
full_text:
Khalifah was an impoverished, merry fisherman of Baghdad who lived in a ruined hut and owned only a patched net and a single linen tunic with ragged sleeves. Despite his poverty, he was celebrated across the riverfront for his comical songs and cheerful disposition.

One morning, having cast his net four times without catching a single fish, Khalifah cast for the fifth time, and dragged up an intelligent ape wearing a silver collar!

The ape signaled that he wished to be the fisherman’s partner. Guided by the ape’s gestures, Khalifah cast his net in a secret eddy and caught two magnificent royal carps of shimmering gold. The ape directed him to take the fish to the grand palace of the Caliph.

That afternoon, the Caliph Harun al-Rashid, walking disguised as an ordinary boatman on the Tigris, met Khalifah. Amused by the fisherman’s comical banter, the Caliph proposed a partnership: 'Let us fish together, brother, and divide the catch!'

They cast the net, and caught a silver chest containing precious gems!

The Caliph, delighted by Khalifah’s complete lack of greed—for the fisherman insisted on dividing every coin equally and giving the larger half to his partner—invited Khalifah to the palace.

When Khalifah saw his humble partner seated upon the golden throne of the Caliphate, he fell to his knees in comical terror!

Harun al-Rashid laughed with imperial joy, raised the fisherman to his feet, appointed him Chief Master of the River Fleet of Baghdad, and made him wealthy for life, proving that pure simplicity and good humor earn the highest rewards.
moral: Good humor, generosity in poverty, and pure simplicity of heart win royal friendship and fortune. [ES]
